question.problem: Find the roots of the polynomial $p(y)=6{y}^{4}+3{y}^{3}-45{y}^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(y)=0,$ that is

$$
6{y}^{4}+3{y}^{3}-45{y}^{2}=0.
$$

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $3{y}^{2}.$ We can factor out the $3{y}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{y}^{2}(2{y}^{2}+y-15) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $2{y}^{2}+y-15$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{y}^{2}(2{y}^{2}+y-15) & =0 \\ 3{y}^{2}(y+3)(2y-5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $y=0,$ $y=-3,$ and $y=\frac{5}{2}.$
